## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One issue should be fixed: the new adopt branch rewrites the config file and reports a change even when the incoming value equals the current one. This breaks the module's promise to preserve untouched files.

## Changes
This PR adds an `adopt` flag to `merge`. When it is set, every incoming key that already exists is overwritten and recorded in the change list. The `replace` path moves into its own branch, and two tests cover adopt and replace when the incoming value is different.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/config.py:13 — correctness — Skip adopted keys whose value is already equal — With `adopt=True`, calling `merge(path, {"theme": "dark"})` on a file containing `{"theme":"dark"}\n` returns `["theme"]` and rewrites the file with `indent=2`. Unlike the `replace` branch at lines 18-21, the `adopt` branch does not check `current[key] != value`. The same happens when both flags are set, because `adopt` is checked first. The added `test_adopt_updates_setting` only uses a different value, so no test covers the equal-value case. — When adopt mode runs on settings that are already up to date, it reports false changes and reformats files the module docstring says it preserves. — Fix: Apply the `current[key] != value` guard used by `replace`, and add an adopt counterpart to `test_unchanged_replacement_preserves_bytes`.
